prompt: A stationary firework of mass 0.80 kg explodes in mid-air into exactly two fragments. Fragment 1 of mass 0.30 kg travels east at 24 m s^-1. What are the speed and direction of motion of fragment 2 immediately after the explosion?

answer.explanation: Mass of fragment 2 = 0.80 kg - 0.30 kg = 0.50 kg. Initial momentum is zero. Momentum of fragment 1 = 0.30 kg x 24 m s^-1 = 7.2 kg m s^-1 east. By conservation of momentum, fragment 2 must have momentum 7.2 kg m s^-1 west. Speed = 7.2 kg m s^-1 / 0.50 kg = 14.4 m s^-1.

distractor_explanations: Correct: m_2 = 0.50 kg; p_2 = 7.2 kg m s^-1 west; v_2 = 7.2 / 0.50 = 14.4 m s^-1 west.
Assumes both fragments fly off at the same speed despite having different masses.
Momentum must oppose fragment 1 to sum to zero initial momentum.
hints: Find the mass of the second fragment first.
Total momentum before the explosion was zero.
